name: autonomic
description: Autopilot as a Claude Code mod. In autopilot (AUTONOMIC_MODE=autopilot per spawn, or /autopilot on) a global policy joins the system prompt; each AskUserQuestion and each permission ask is judged against the policy and the session's scope, every decision is appended to a ledger, and a signal left with the operator reaches them by toast, band and an optional bell. A turn end is never judged, blocked or continued. Fails toward manual. Requires Claude Code 2.1.289 or later.

policyPath.title: Policy file
policyPath.description: The autopilot standing orders. Written with the default on first start; edit it freely.

bell.title: Bell command
bell.description: A shell command run on each pain signal, with AUTONOMIC_MESSAGE set to one line, for example: curl -d "$AUTONOMIC_MESSAGE" ntfy.sh/<topic>. AUTONOMIC_BELL on a spawn overrides it. Unset: toast and band only.

decidingModel.title: Deciding model
decidingModel.description: When set (for example claude-sonnet-5-5), every judgment is a plain completion on this model: it sees the prompt alone, no transcript. Unset: the judge forks the session's own model, as before.

neverApprove.title: Never-approve rules
neverApprove.description: In autopilot, a command whose own words match one of these always reaches you, even under bypass permissions; a match found only in text (a message, a quoted argument, an interpreter's script) goes to the fork with the finding. Remove a name to let the fork judge it. Known: force-push default-branch-push no-verify ai-trailer. Retired in 0.10.0, now judged: branch-delete rm-outside unreadable — a setting that names them still loads. Empty: none.

readers.title: Reader commands
readers.description: Command prefixes, separated by ;, that name a file but never run it. A reader that names a file a command just wrote does not keep that file's words for the never-approve list. Add your own, for example: gh pr create; gh pr edit; gh issue create; gh issue comment; herdr agent prompt. Empty: none.
readers.default: gh pr create; gh pr edit; gh issue create; gh issue comment
